chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, who said: Aiman ibn Mahraz narrated to us, from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The names of Mecca are five: Umm al-Qura, Mecca, Bakkah, and Bassasah. As for Bassasah, it is because when they oppressed its people, they were expelled and destroyed from it. And Umm Ruhm, because when they adhered to it, they were shown mercy.

key_terms.أُمُّ الْقُرَى: Mother of all settlements (a name for Mecca)
key_terms.أُمُّ رَحْمٍ: Mother of Mercy, referring to divine mercy for those who stay
key_terms.الْبَسَّاسَةُ: The name referring to the act of expelling and destroying oppressors

ai.seo_question: What are the five names of Mecca and their meanings according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the five names of Mecca, highlighting 'Bassasah' as the place where oppressors are expelled and destroyed, and 'Uamm Ruhm' as the abode of mercy for those who seek refuge. This narration, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, underscores the dual spiritual and historical nature of the sanctuary as both a place of divine protection and retribution, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the city's sacred geography and its role in Islamic eschatology.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-22 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, on the authority of Aiman ibn Mohraz, on the authority of Muawiyah ibn Ammar that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,

“Mecca has five names. They are, ‘Ummul Qura , Mecca, Becca, Bassasa since anyone who performed any acts of oppression there was deported from it and destroyed, and ‘Umma Ruhm since they had mercy with whomever took refuge there.”
